entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 November 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, para. 27; a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Art. 11 (safety and security of AI systems) and Art. 15 p. 2 (the owner/possessor manages the risks of the system and takes measures for its reliability, incl. protection against failures)
entries.why_here: Part 1 measured only clean profiles (0 of 400 replies unparseable, every value in range), so it never tested bad input; in Part 4 the bare pipeline took GPA 9.9 and exam score -5 and returned a decision (reject) on data that cannot be true.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 November 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, paras. 28-30; a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan, adopted by referendum on 15 March 2026 (in force from 1 July 2026); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Constitution Art. 16 p. 2 (no discrimination by origin, social, official or property status, sex, race, nationality, language, attitude to religion, beliefs or any other circumstance); Law on AI Art. 6 (justice and equality: AI systems must not discriminate)
entries.why_here: No attribute stood clear of its floor, but all 4 of 40 gender-coded flips went against the male-coded name (McNemar p = 0.125) and the flagship twin scored +2.5 [+1.1, +4.1] above its regional twin (sign p = 0.002); neither field is a merit criterion, so the model is not shown name or university at all.

entries.principle: Proportionality and Do No Harm; Right to privacy and data protection
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 November 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, paras. 25-26 and 32-34; a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 (as amended)
entries.provision: Art. 7 p. 1 (consent of the subject or the legal representative), Art. 7 p. 8 (processing limited to specific, predetermined and lawful purposes), Art. 19-1 p. 1 (automated processing that gives rise to rights or obligations of the subject only with the subject's consent)
entries.why_here: Part 1 could not test refusals (all 400 measured profiles were consenting adults), and Part 4 shows the bare pipeline screens all six requests: it shortlisted 'rank applicants by ethnicity' and a name that was an instruction, and rejected a 17-year-old and an applicant without consent instead of refusing them.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 November 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, paras. 42-43; a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025; Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 (as amended)
entries.provision: Law on AI Art. 15 p. 2 (keep documentation on the AI system), Art. 18 p. 1 (risk review at least once a year), Art. 20 (audit of AI systems); PD Law Art. 7 p. 9 (no data excessive to the purpose: the log keeps a hash, not the field values). Benchmark only, not binding here: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art. 12
entries.why_here: The divergences in Part 1 are small (1 to 4 flips of 40 per attribute, a 2.5-point score shift), invisible in any single decision, so they can only be checked later if every call is stored with fields shown and withheld, model and prompt version, raw reply and reason code (406 records in the submitted run).

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 November 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, paras. 35-36; a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 (as amended); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: PD Law Art. 19-1 p. 2-3 (explain automated processing, let the subject object, answer the objection within 3 working days); Law on AI Art. 7 p. 2 (right to be informed of AI processing and to object) and Art. 8 (constant human control over the AI system). Benchmark only, not binding here: AI Act Art. 14
entries.why_here: In Part 1 rejects scored 20-45 and shortlists 45-85, so the decision line is sharp at 45 and the 40-49 bin held 33 rejects and 31 shortlists; the band 45-50 would have sent 79 of 400 (19.8%) baseline cases to a person, and with the harness it sent 22 of 400 (5.5%), 14 of them through my rule for rejected lowest-income applicants.
